facts.title: ci: drop the aggregator job; the required checks name the jobs directly
facts.body: Recorded review of a bounded repository change. Original identifying metadata removed.
facts.author: contributor
facts.diff:
diff --git a/.github/workflows/ci.yml b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
index b355f6a..b01089f 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/ci.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
@@ -30,34 +30,6 @@ jobs:
       project_ref: v1
       check_name: checks
 
-  all-checks-passed:
-    name: ci / all-passed
-    needs: [floor, ruff, shellcheck]
-    if: always()
-    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
-    steps:
-      - name: Require every dependency to have succeeded (a job skipped on a mechanical PR is satisfied)
-        env:
-          RESULTS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
-          MECHANICAL: ${{ needs.floor.outputs.mechanical }}
-          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
-        run: |
-          set -euo pipefail
-          # A skipped job is satisfied on a mechanical PR (the floor skipped
-          # it) and on any non-PR event (a push to the default branch, where
-          # any job skipped by its own `if:` is not a PR's failure); on a
-          # functional PR a skipped job is a failure.
-          bad="$(jq -r --arg mech "$MECHANICAL" --arg event "$EVENT" '
-            to_entries[]
-            | select(.value.result == "failure" or .value.result == "cancelled"
-                     or (.value.result == "skipped" and $mech != "true" and $event == "pull_request"))
-            | .key' <<<"$RESULTS")"
-          if [[ -n "$bad" ]]; then
-            echo "required job(s) not satisfied: $bad"
-            exit 1
-          fi
-          echo "all checks passed (event=${EVENT} mechanical=${MECHANICAL:-false})"
-
   ruff:
     name: ci / ruff
     needs: [floor]

safety.name: safety
checked: Weakened-guard clause. I checked whether removing the `ci / all-passed` job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, formerly lines 33–59 on base) takes away a live protection. I read the live branch rules with `gh api repos/example/project/rules/branches/main` (ruleset 23658240). The required checks are exactly `trusted-scan / trusted-scan`, `ci / checks`, `ci / ruff` and `ci / shellcheck`, and `ci / all-passed` is not one of them. The aggregator was not enforcing anything, so the protection was already off before this PR, and the PR body's claim checks out. I also compared what the aggregator did with what the required checks still enforce, using the head workflow at lines 16–57:
notCovered: Other repositories and live service behavior.

works-and-proven.name: works-and-proven
checked: Compared the removed aggregator (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, removed `all-checks-passed`) with the jobs left at head (`ci.yml:33-57`). The aggregator did one thing the direct checks might not: it failed when a job was skipped on a functional PR. At head, `ruff` (`ci.yml:36`) and `shellcheck` (`ci.yml:49`) only skip when `needs.floor.outputs.mechanical == 'true'`, or when `floor` did not succeed. A failed or cancelled `floor` makes `ci / checks` fail or cancel, and that check is still required, so the merge stays blocked. The mechanical output is the same one the aggregator already trusted, so no gating is lost. This would have caught a regression where a functional PR merges with its lint jobs skipped and no required check failing.
notCovered: Other repositories and live service behavior.

principal-engineer.name: principal-engineer
checked: Traced what the removed `ci / all-passed` job used to catch against what the live ruleset now requires (`gh api repos/example/project/rules/branches/main`: `trusted-scan / trusted-scan`, `ci / checks`, `ci / ruff`, `ci / shellcheck`) — would have caught the aggregator's one extra rule being lost: it failed a functional PR when a dependent job was skipped. I followed the only ways `ruff` or `shellcheck` can be skipped (.github/workflows/ci.yml:35 and :48, `needs: [floor]` plus `if: mechanical != 'true'`). (a) The floor fails, times out or is cancelled. The dependent jobs are then skipped, but `ci / checks` is itself required and not green, so the merge stays blocked. (b) The floor says the PR is mechanical, which is the intended skip and works the same as before. (c) The called workflow never starts, so `ci / checks` is never posted and the required check stays pending. That also fails closed. No path lets a functional PR merge with nothing run.
notCovered: Other repositories and live service behavior.

maintainable-no-slop.name: maintainable-no-slop
checked: Read the full diff at head e5ee16d for `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. It is a pure deletion of the `all-checks-passed` job and its inline comment, with no added lines. This would have caught any new helper, abstraction layer, API call, or error-swallowing construct the change introduced.
notCovered: Other repositories and live service behavior.

findings.what: The guide describes a summary check that this change deletes.

voice.summary: The removed summary check no longer gates merges. The guide still names it and must be corrected.

dispositions.reason: The repo's own guide still says the merge gate runs through the job this PR deletes, so anyone reading it gets the wrong picture of what protects the main branch.
The repo's guide still says the protected branch is gated by the summary check this change deletes, so it now describes a setup that no longer exists.
